learning_outcomes.text: Be original in the development and application of ideas, within a research environment.
Solution of problem in new and unfamiliar multidisciplinary environments, related to its knowledge area.
Integration of knowledge, facing the complexity of issuing judgments and sentences parting from some information that includes ethic and social liability constraints.
Ability of communicating justified decisions and conclusions, to specialized and unspecialized listeners.
Ability of autonomous learning.
Critical analysis of the information coming from the sensing and instrumentation subsystems.
Practical and experimental verification of monitoring and controlling electrical energy conversion systems, including safety operation of electric systems
Skills related to teamwork, recognizing different roles within a group and different ways of organizing research teams.
Ability to manage information: search, analysis and synthesis of the specific technical information.
Ability to assimilate and communicate information in English concerning technical documents.
Ability to plan and organize work
Skills for critical reasoning, making decisions and making judgments based on information that include reflecting on social and ethical responsibilities of professional activity
Concern for quality and achievement motivation
Understanding of the importance and the area of utilization of electrical power systems for generation, transmission and distribution of electrical energy.
Ability to understand the basics of the dynamic modelling of electrical power systems.
Identification of the main characteristics, design strategies and the constructive elements and materials of the Electrical Power Systems.
Understand the importance of control and monitoring systems in electrical power systems.
Analyse the different grid connection strategies from a technical and economic point of view.
Identify the technical-economic legislation and regulations at different levels (local, regional, national, European, etc.) applicable to electrical power systems.

Knowing and analysing the energy structures and technologies that guarantee the supply of the determined demand, analysing future energy needs and possible technological solutions, taking into account criteria of efficiency, security, guarantee of supply and environmental implications.
Identify the agents participating in the electricity and gas market, as well as their operation, taking into account different management methodologies.
Understand the price formation process, understanding the different components of the final price of electricity and tariffs.
Knowing the construction and design aspects, as well as the principle of operation of the main types of electricity generation plants, both conventional and non-conventional.
To understand the difference between distributed and centralised generation and to identify the different design criteria for both types of generation systems.
Knowing the elements involved in the protection of power plants as well as their protection criteria.
To understand the operation of the different types of power plants.

syllabus_topics: Wind, solar thermal, photovoltaic, fuel cells, biomass and MSW, tidal and wave power, microturbines,...
assessment_rules: The evaluation percentages for the written exam (15% to 40%), oral exams (15% to 40%), works and projects (20% to 50%), practical cases (10% to 30%), and observation techniques (10% to 20%) will be specified at the beginning of the sessions. For differentiated assessment, each case will be studied, and a compatible assessment will be proposed according to specific conditions and University rules.
